recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit. Future assertedDate boundary work should be handled under the relevant FHIR Extension Pack issues or later Jira keys rather than by duplicating or rewording the current core Condition.recordedDate comment.
issue_request: FHIR-27808 was a Published/Persuasive R5 Patient Care clarification asking for Condition.recordedDate to say that receiving systems should preferably preserve a sending-system recordedDate when provided, and may assert their own system-generated date when it is not provided.
initial_application: Git commit eef7e67022 explicitly applied J#27808 by adding the requested comment and committee note to source/condition/structuredefinition-Condition.xml. Later commit 7fc5cd4fe9, for FHIR-34392/FHIR-34394, retained the preservation/defaulting semantics while adding onset-proxy rationale and changing the fallback wording to receipt timestamp.
additional_context: Condition is active in source/fhir.ini, so the Condition StructureDefinition is build-scope source. Later Published issues FHIR-34392 and FHIR-34394 refined the same recordedDate comment; FHIR-34395 temporarily removed the recorder contrast only when recorder was replaced by participant, and the combined branch already contains FHIR-34394 reconciliation restoring that contrast after recorder returned. FHIR-33180 concerns the condition-assertedDate extension in the FHIR Extension Pack and confirms the assertedDate/recordedDate distinction without requiring a core recordedDate edit.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current Condition.recordedDate short and comment already convey the FHIR-27808 rule as later refined: recordedDate is the first recorded date, a provided sending-system recordedDate should be preserved, and if one is not provided the receiving-system receipt timestamp may be used as the recordedDate.
